cards.title: START Triage
cards.body:
**RPM** — Respirations, Perfusion, Mental status.

- **RED / IMMEDIATE:** breathing but RR >30 or <8, capillary refill >2 s or weak radial pulse, cannot follow commands.
- **YELLOW / DELAYED:** breathing, normal perfusion, follows commands, but cannot walk.
- **GREEN / MINOR:** walking wounded.
- **BLACK / EXPECTANT:** not breathing after opening the airway; no pulse. In a mass-casualty event, do not start CPR on a clearly dead patient when resources are overwhelmed.

Re-triage every few minutes. Treat life threats in this order: massive bleeding, airway, breathing, circulation, hypothermia.

cards.title: CPR
cards.body:
**Adult:** 30 compressions : 2 breaths, 100–120/min, depth 5–6 cm, allow full recoil. **Child:** 15:2 (if alone, 30:2), depth about 5 cm. **Infant:** 15:2, two fingers, depth about 4 cm.

Use an AED as soon as available; follow its prompts. If unwilling/unable to give breaths, do compression-only CPR. Swap compressors every 2 minutes. Do not stop for anything other than an AED, obvious signs of life, or physical exhaustion.

cards.title: Massive Bleeding
cards.body:
1. Direct, firm pressure with gauze; add layers, do not lift.
2. Pack deep wounds firmly, then hold pressure.
3. Tourniquet for life-threatening limb bleeding: 5–7 cm above the wound (not over a joint), tighten until bleeding stops, **write the time**.
4. Do not loosen a tourniquet once applied unless directed by a clinician.
5. Treat shock: lay flat, keep warm, no food/drink.

cards.title: Anaphylaxis
cards.body: **Epinephrine first.** Adult 0.3–0.5 mg IM outer thigh; child 0.01 mg/kg IM (max 0.15 mg if <15 kg); 15–30 kg junior 0.15 mg autoinjector. Use the 1 mg/mL (1:1,000) IM formulation, never dilute IV epinephrine. Repeat after 5–15 minutes if needed. Call emergency services. Lay the patient flat with legs raised unless breathing is difficult; do not stand them up. Antihistamines are not a substitute for epinephrine.

cards.title: Hypothermia
cards.body: Move to shelter, remove wet clothes, insulate from the ground, warm the **trunk** first. Use skin-to-skin or dry blankets. Warm sweet drinks only if fully alert. **No alcohol, no rubbing, no hot water.** Handle gently. Severe hypothermia (confusion, stiff muscles, slow pulse) is a hospital emergency — do not let the patient walk.

cards.title: Heat Illness
cards.body:
**Heat exhaustion:** heavy sweating, weakness, nausea, headache. Move to shade, loosen clothing, fan, cool with water, sip ORS.

**Heat stroke:** confusion, hot dry or wet skin, collapse, temperature >40 °C. **Cool immediately** with cold water/ice packs to neck, armpits, groin; call emergency services. Do not give fluids to an unconscious person.

cards.title: Burns
cards.body: Cool with clean running water for **20 minutes**. Remove jewellery/loose clothing before swelling. Cover with clean non-stick dressing. **No ice, butter, oil or toothpaste.** Estimate area with the patient's palm ≈1%. Rule of nines: head 9%, each arm 9%, front trunk 18%, back trunk 18%, each leg 18%. Seek care for >10% area, face/hands/genitals, electrical, chemical, or inhalation burns.

cards.title: Snakebite
cards.body: Move away from the snake. Keep the patient calm and still; immobilise the limb at or slightly below heart level. Remove rings/watch. **Do not cut, suck, burn, apply a tight tourniquet, or give alcohol.** For suspected neurotoxic elapid bites (e.g. Australia, parts of Asia/Africa), a firm pressure-immobilisation bandage and complete immobilisation may be advised by local protocol — apply only if trained. Note time and appearance. Evacuate to hospital; antivenom is the treatment.

cards.title: Stroke — FAST
cards.body: **F**ace droop. **A**rm weakness. **S**peech difficulty. **T**ime to call emergency services. Note the time symptoms began; thrombolysis is time-critical. Do not give food or drink. Keep the airway clear.

cards.title: Seizure
cards.body: Protect the head, clear dangerous objects, do not restrain or put anything in the mouth. Time the seizure. After it ends, place the patient in the recovery position. Call emergency services if >5 minutes, repeated seizures, injury, pregnancy, diabetes, or it is a first seizure.

cards.title: Choking
cards.body: **Adult/child:** 5 back blows, then 5 abdominal thrusts; repeat. **Infant:** 5 back blows, then 5 chest thrusts. If unconscious, start CPR. See a clinician after abdominal thrusts.

cards.title: Oral Rehydration (ORS)
cards.body: WHO low-osmolarity formula per **1 litre clean water**: 2.6 g salt, 13.5 g glucose, 1.5 g potassium chloride (where available). Household approximation: **6 level teaspoons table sugar + ½ level teaspoon salt per litre** (6 tsp sugar ≈ 25 g sucrose ≈ the 13.5 g glucose target). Stir until dissolved. Sip frequently. Do not add extra salt or use sports drinks as a substitute. Stop and seek help for persistent vomiting, blood in stool, or severe lethargy. Infants and severely dehydrated patients need medical supervision.

cards.title: Boiling Water
cards.body: Bring to a **rolling boil for 1 minute** below 2,000 m (6,500 ft); **3 minutes** above. Let it cool covered. Boiling kills pathogens; it does not remove chemicals, heavy metals or radiation particles. Filter cloudy water first for taste and efficacy.

cards.title: Bleach Disinfection
cards.body: Use plain unscented household bleach. **5.25–6%:** 2 drops/litre clear, 4 drops/litre cloudy. **8.25%:** 1 drop/litre clear, 2 drops/litre cloudy. Stir and wait **30 minutes** (60 if cloudy/cold). Water should have a faint chlorine smell; if not, repeat once. Do not use scented, splashless, or additive bleach. Filter first if cloudy. Boiling or certified filtration is preferred.

cards.title: Water Planning
cards.body: Minimum **4 L/person/day** for drinking + basic hygiene; 6–8 L in heat. Store 14 days if possible. Use food-grade containers, label and rotate every 6 months. Keep out of sunlight. Never drink floodwater or water from a damaged municipal system without treatment.

cards.title: Fire Triangle
cards.body: **Tinder → kindling → fuel.** Prepare three sizes before striking. Start small, protect from wind, feed gradually. Have water/dirt ready. **Never burn charcoal or use a generator indoors** — carbon monoxide kills. In a shelter, maintain ventilation and a CO alarm.

cards.title: Shelter Priorities
cards.body: 1. Get out of wind and rain. 2. Insulate from the ground (branches, leaves, pad). 3. Keep dry. 4. Avoid dead standing trees and flash-flood ground. 5. Mark your location. A small shelter warmed by body heat beats a large cold one. Ventilate if using fire.

cards.title: Distress Signals
cards.body: **Three of anything** is a distress signal: three whistle blasts, three fires, three flashes, three gunshots (where legal/safe). Use a signal mirror, bright marker, and ground-to-air symbols. SOS is **... --- ...**. Stay put once you have signalled unless staying is more dangerous; searchers will converge on your location.

cards.title: Compass & Declination
cards.body: **True bearing = magnetic bearing + east declination** (or − west declination). The console computes WMM2025 declination for your position. Set the map/compass to the same reference. Aim off when navigating around obstacles. Always carry a paper map and a spare compass.

cards.title: Pace Count
cards.body: Measure 100 m. Walk it naturally and count every second step (or both steps); repeat three times and average. Recalibrate on slopes, sand, snow and with a pack. Use ranger beads to track hundreds. Typical adult: 60–70 double-paces per 100 m.

cards.title: Sun & Stars
cards.body: **Northern hemisphere:** at solar noon the sun is due south; shadows point north. At night, Polaris (North Star) is due north at an altitude equal to your latitude. **Southern hemisphere:** use the Southern Cross — extend the long axis 4.5× and drop to the horizon for south. The sun rises east and sets west; it is only exactly east/west at the equinox.

cards.title: Nowcasting
cards.body: Falling pressure >3.5 hPa in 3 h = rapid deterioration. Rising = improving. Cumulonimbus, sudden wind shifts, and a dark green sky mean severe weather. Count seconds between lightning and thunder; **<30 s = take shelter now** (lightning can strike 16 km from the storm).

cards.title: Radiation Protection
cards.body: **Time, distance, shielding.** Dose falls roughly with the square of distance and with shielding mass. Get inside, go to the basement or core of the building, shut off ventilation, seal gaps. Remove outer clothing and shower after exposure. Use KI only when directed; it protects the thyroid only. Record dose rate and time.

cards.title: Fallout Decay (7:10)
cards.body: For early fallout, dose rate falls by about a factor of 10 for every 7× increase in time after detonation (t^-1.2). Example: 1,000 µSv/h at H+1 → ~100 µSv/h at H+7 → ~10 µSv/h at H+49. This is an approximation; measure with an instrument and shelter.

cards.title: KI Dosing (FDA)
cards.body: Adults (including pregnant/lactating): **130 mg**. Children 3–18 y: **65 mg**. 1 month–3 y: **32 mg**. Birth–1 month: **16 mg**. Every 24 h while exposure continues, **only when directed by authorities** unless the risk clearly outweighs the risk of thyroid cancer. Do not use if iodine-allergic. KI is not a general radiation antidote.

cards.title: Decontamination
cards.body: Remove outer clothing (most contamination) and bag it. Brush off dry particles before wetting. Shower with lukewarm water and soap; do not scrub hard or use hot water. Flush eyes/nose/mouth. Cover any wound. Do not eat, drink or smoke until decontaminated. Seek monitoring.

cards.title: Field Knots
cards.body: **Bowline** — fixed loop that will not slip. **Clove hitch** — quick attachment to a post. **Taut-line hitch** — adjustable tension. **Figure-eight** — stopper. **Square/reef** — binding packages (not for load-bearing). **Sheet bend** — join unequal ropes. **Prusik** — friction hitch. **Trucker's hitch** — mechanical advantage. Practise in the dark with gloves.

cards.title: Field Sanitation
cards.body: Latrine: at least **30 m (100 ft) from water**, 1 m deep, cover after each use. Keep a handwashing station with soap and water. Disinfect shared surfaces. Store waste away from shelter. A 5% bleach solution (1 part bleach : 9 parts water) for surfaces; let contact 10 minutes. Never mix bleach with ammonia or acid.

cards.title: Food Safety
cards.body: Keep hot food >60 °C and cold food <4 °C. Discard food left >2 h at room temperature (1 h above 32 °C). Boil or peel produce. Cook meat thoroughly. Do not eat unknown plants or mushrooms — misidentification can be fatal. Ration 2,000 kcal/person/day as a baseline; do not restrict water to save food.

cards.title: Backup Power Safety
cards.body: **Never** run a generator indoors, in a garage, or near windows — CO is invisible. Do not backfeed a house; use a transfer switch. Fuse every circuit. Keep batteries ventilated and away from metal. **Lithium-ion battery fires:** copious water to cool from a safe distance if trained; do not rely on smothering alone. **Lithium-metal cells:** use a Class D extinguisher or dry sand; never water. Size the battery bank for depth of discharge and cold temperature.

cards.title: MAYDAY Call
cards.body:
**MAYDAY, MAYDAY, MAYDAY** — this is [vessel/callsign] — position [lat/lon or MGRS] — nature of distress — number of persons — assistance required — over.

For marine VHF use Ch 16; aviation 121.5; use the highest power and clearest location. If no answer, repeat. Conserve battery; monitor the emergency channel.

cards.title: Radio Discipline
cards.body: Listen before transmitting. Identify with your callsign. Keep messages short and factual. Use plain language; use prowords correctly. **Never** transmit false distress calls. On shared nets, use **BREAK** for priority traffic. Write down frequencies, times and stations. Encryption is not a substitute for good OPSEC.

cards.title: Field Security
cards.body: Establish a baseline, then watch for changes. Use the **OODA loop** (Observe, Orient, Decide, Act). Avoid patterns; vary routes and times. Keep a low profile, secure documents, and share information on a need-to-know basis. In a crowd, identify exits and cover. De-escalate; violence is a last resort and a legal matter.

cards.title: Operational Security
cards.body: Assume any electronic device can be lost, seized or tracked. Keep an encrypted vault for sensitive notes. Do not post locations, movements, stockpiles or routes. Use paper for critical plans. Strip metadata from photos before sharing. Have a duress plan and a trusted contact who knows your check-in schedule.

cards.title: Stress & Decision Making
cards.body: Under stress, breathing and heart rate rise and peripheral vision narrows. Use **box breathing** (4 s in, 4 s hold, 4 s out, 4 s hold). Name the problem out loud. Set a decision deadline. Rotate rest. Sleep is a survival requirement, not a luxury. Watch for tunnel vision and normalcy bias.

cards.title: Personal Hygiene
cards.body: Wash hands before food and after waste. Brush teeth with safe water. Keep feet dry and inspect daily. Treat blisters early. Disinfect wounds immediately. Launder or sun-dry clothing. Menstrual and infant supplies are critical, not optional. Body lice and scabies spread in crowded shelters.

cards.title: Fire Extinguisher — PASS
cards.body: **P**ull the pin. **A**im at the base of the fire. **S**queeze the handle. **S**weep side to side. Only fight a small fire with a clear exit behind you. Never use water on electrical or grease fires. Get out and call emergency services if the fire grows.

cards.title: Earthquake
cards.body: **Drop, cover, hold on.** Stay away from windows and heavy objects. If in bed, stay and protect your head. If outdoors, move to open ground. If driving, pull over away from bridges/lines. After shaking, expect aftershocks, check for gas leaks, and avoid damaged structures. Near the coast, move to high ground immediately — do not wait for a warning.

cards.title: Flood
cards.body: Move to higher ground early. **Never walk or drive through moving water** — 15 cm can knock you down, 30 cm can float a vehicle. Assume floodwater is contaminated with sewage and chemicals. Boil or filter all drinking water. Avoid downed power lines. Document damage for insurance.

cards.title: Water Scarcity
cards.body: Prioritise drinking water; reduce bathing and cleaning. Reuse greywater for flushing (not drinking). Harvest rain where legal and safe. Protect stored water from heat and sunlight. Know your community water point and carry containers. Dehydration signs: dark urine, dizziness, confusion.
